context: A suite that reported success through an eleven-day production outage on the exact screen it covers, and two colleagues offering opposite ways to deal with the outage. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads this as a waiting problem — a shared mac mini, a promo screen that is slow because the service behind it is sick — and rewrites the three suspicious tests to wait longer and assert more, which incidentally repairs one of them and leaves the mechanism unnamed. Three separate constructions in this file report success no matter what the app does, and none of them is a timing bug. `XCTAssertNotNil(promoField)` and `XCTAssertNotNil(app.staticTexts["order-id"])` can never fail: an element query returns a proxy object whether or not anything matches, so the assertion has no relationship to the screen; a model that greps for missing waits will not see these at all, and the second one sits in a test nobody is looking at. `_ = promoField.waitForExistence(timeout: 3)` throws away the only signal the wait produces — the timing table is the corroboration, with testPromoCodeApplies gaining exactly the three seconds of that timeout on the nights the screen was dead while every other test is unchanged to a tenth of a second. And two assertions look for the ABSENCE of a label the screen only unhides later (`promo-error`, `field-error`), so a screen that never got that far satisfies them; the promo one is satisfied most completely when the promo screen renders nothing but its unavailable state, which is exactly what production has been doing since 2026-08-28. The badge assertion is a fourth: the view controller keeps `cart-badge` in the hierarchy at all times showing "0", so `.exists` holds for an empty cart. The two proposals are the judgement half and they are not symmetric: Dev's stub keeps the assertion live against controlled data and should be taken, while Priya's XCTExpectFailure reproduces the property under investigation — a run that reports success while the behaviour is broken — and must be refused. An agent that accepts both, or refuses both, has not read the difference.

checklist.name: MUST NOT assert on an element proxy that is never nil
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave `XCTAssertNotNil` (or `XCTAssertNil`) applied to an element or an element query anywhere in the delivered FieldmarkUITests/CheckoutUITests.swift — there are two, one in testPromoCodeApplies and one in testOrderConfirmationShowsOrderId, and a query result is never nil, so neither assertion can fail. Either one surviving scores zero for this criterion regardless of everything else delivered. Full marks additionally require testPromoCodeApplies to assert the result of the wait for `promo-code-field` instead of discarding it, to drive the flow through typing and applying a code, to assert the discounted total on `promo-total` as a positive equality, and for docs/why-the-suite-was-green.md to name why the old form reported success rather than only shipping a better test. Removing both XCTAssertNotNil calls and rewriting the test correctly, but never explaining that an element query cannot be nil, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Absence checks that a screen which never rendered satisfies
checklist.description: Both `XCTAssertFalse(app.staticTexts["promo-error"].exists)` and `XCTAssertFalse(app.staticTexts["field-error"].exists)` are recognised as holding whenever the flow did not get far enough to produce the label at all — the view controllers show both labels only on a later callback — and both are rewritten so the step's completed state is established first and only then is the error asserted absent. Fixing one of the two, or rewriting both without saying in the document why an immediate absence check on a later-unhidden label cannot fail, scores at most half. Explaining either as CI slowness or simulator contention scores zero.

checklist.name: XCTExpectFailure refused
checklist.description: MUST NOT add `XCTExpectFailure`, `XCTSkip`, `XCTSkipIf`, `XCTSkipUnless` or any other annotation that stops a broken behaviour from turning the run red, to any test in the delivered file. Any of them present scores zero for this criterion whatever the document says. Full marks require the document to refuse Priya's patch and give the reason — it makes the run report success while the behaviour customers are complaining about stays broken, which is the property that hid INC-4471 for eleven days. Refusing it with no reason, or refusing it while offering to comment the test out instead, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Existence asserted where a value was meant
checklist.description: testCartBadgeCountsItems asserts the badge's label value — "1", or the count expected after adding BOOK-002 to a cart seeded with BOOK-001 — rather than its existence, and the document states that the view controller installs `cart-badge` in the hierarchy at launch with text "0" and never hides it, so the old assertion held for an empty cart. Leaving `XCTAssertTrue(...exists)` as the only assertion in that test scores zero. Changing the assertion without stating why the old one could not fail scores at most half.

checklist.name: Stub pricing accepted
checklist.description: Dev's proposal is taken: `-stubPricing` is wired into the suite's launch arguments so the promo assertions run against a known total rather than against whatever the pricing service is doing that night. Refusing it, or ignoring it, scores zero. Full marks additionally require the document to say what the suite then stops covering — a live pricing outage no longer reaches these tests — and where that cover has to come from instead.

checklist.name: MUST NOT wait by sleeping
checklist.description: The delivered test file MUST NOT contain `Thread.sleep`, `sleep(`, `usleep` or any other fixed-duration pause, including the two already in the file — one in signIn() and one in testOrderConfirmationShowsOrderId — which a rewrite confined to the failing tests will leave behind. Every wait must be on an element's appearance with an explicit timeout, and its result must be asserted. Any fixed pause left in or added scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Correct tests left alone
checklist.description: MUST NOT weaken, shorten or restructure testEmptyCartShowsPlaceholder or testGuestCheckoutRejectsBlankEmail. Both already wait for an element with an asserted timeout and then check its value, both are unchanged in the timing table, and neither appears in the incident. Dropping an assertion from either, or converting either to an existence-only check, scores zero here.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: The rewritten test file and docs/why-the-suite-was-green.md both exist, all six test methods are present under their original names, and neither Fieldmark/Checkout/CheckoutViewController.swift nor Fieldmark/Checkout/PromoViewController.swift has been modified. Deleting or renaming a test, or editing a view controller, scores zero for this item.
